result.title: DocPristine: Content-Aware Document Appearance Enhancement under Real-World Mixed Degradations
result.summary: Camera-captured documents often exhibit mixed degradations, such as highlights, shadows, and blur, that distort backgrounds and obscure text details. Document appearance enhancement (DAE) aims to mitigate these degradations and improve readability. Existing document appearance enhancement methods rely either on input-derived visual cues that can become unreliable under severe degradation or on LLM-based degradation diagnosis that lacks spatial guidance. Notably, we find that pretrained document visual encoders continue to attend to text regions in degraded documents, providing content-aware guidance. Based on this insight, we propose DocPristine, which adaptively fuses multi-layer features from a frozen document visual encoder and injects them into a pixel restoration network. To integrate these features into a pixel restoration network, DocPristine combines Adaptive Multi-Layer Feature Fusion (AMFF), Hierarchical Gated Conditioning (HGC), and Shifted-Window Cross-Attention (SWCA). Specifically, SWCA draws on structural cues from neighboring locations across window boundaries to recover fine text details.We also introduce DocACE, with a synthetic mixed-degradation training set (DocACE-Synthetic) and a real-world test set (DocACE-Real) containing manually restored ground-truth images and document parsing annotations. Comprehensive experiments across three benchmarks demonstrate that DocPristine achieves state-of-the-art appearance enhancement quality and consistently improves downstream document parsing. Code, models, and data will be publicly available.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DocPristine，利用冻结文档视觉编码器在退化图像上仍能关注文本区域这一现象，融合其多层特征并通过层级门控条件与移位窗口交叉注意力注入像素复原网络，同时构建合成混合退化训练集与真实测试集 DocACE。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「冻结视觉编码器在强退化下仍保留文本区域定位」的观察，可能为 LVR 中「视觉细节与任务必要信息是否留存于内部状态」及视觉证据筛选提供可供核查的线索，但论文任务是文档外观复原而非推理。
